_meta.description: Per-model cost, water, and energy config for AI Water Meter. Replaces the v1 flat TIERS system. See ai-water-meter-v2-prd.md for full sourcing discussion.

waterEnergyMethodology.google-comprehensive: Google's Aug 2025 technical paper (arXiv:2508.15734) / Google Cloud blog: median Gemini Apps text prompt measured at 0.24 Wh energy, 0.26 mL water, full-stack methodology (accelerators + host + idle capacity + datacenter overhead). Paper states this is a blended median across the Gemini Apps fleet for a prompt of roughly 500-700 output tokens; we scale from a 600-token baseline. Applied identically to gemini-3-flash and gemini-3-1-pro since Google did not publish a per-model split — flagged per-model in `notes`.
waterEnergyMethodology.public-estimate-research: University of Rhode Island AI Lab study (reported by Tom's Hardware/DCD, Aug 2025): measured average power draw per response for several deployed models by querying them directly and metering GPU power, not vendor-disclosed. GPT-5: avg 18.35 Wh, up to 40 Wh, for a medium-length ~1000-token response. DeepSeek R1: 20.90 Wh, same ~1000-token baseline. Where we lack a same-model figure (Claude family, gpt-5-4, deepseek-v3/v4-flash), water is derived from energy (or vice versa) using the Wh:mL ratio observed in Google's comprehensive figure (0.24 Wh : 0.26 mL, i.e. mL = Wh x 1.0833), and cross-model scaling uses each model's output-token price relative to a same-family reference model as a rough compute-intensity proxy. All such derived figures are flagged in that model's `notes` field — treat as the weakest-confidence numbers in this file.
waterEnergyMethodology.baseline-note: 'Per-prompt' figures in both source studies are for a single response of a stated token length (600 tok for Google, 1000 tok for the URI study). We scale each source's own stated baseline linearly to a per-million-output-token rate rather than mixing baselines.

_meta.mediaModels: Image/video generation has real vendor $/unit pricing; water/energy is a different problem per unit type. v3 borrowed an unrelated text model's per-token rate scaled by a token-equivalent — a proxy of a proxy, and inaccurate (a diffusion/video model's compute-per-'token' bears no real relationship to an autoregressive text model's). v4 replaces this: every mediaModels entry now carries its own `energyWhPerUnit`/`waterMlPerUnit` grounded in a dedicated per-image or per-second research measurement (see each entry's `sourceUrl`/`notes` — Bertazzini et al. 2506.17016 for image, the video-generation scaling-law paper 2607.04553 for video), not derived from any text model. `tokenEquivalentPerUnit`/`tokenEquivalentSource` are now display-only (the card's 'out-equiv tok' chip) and no longer feed the water/energy math. `inputPricePerMTok` is set only where the vendor actually bills prompt tokens separately (OpenAI's gpt-image family); Google's Imagen/Veo are flat per-unit prices with no separate input charge, so that field is omitted there rather than borrowing a text model's input rate and fabricating a cost Google doesn't bill.
_meta.researchMode: Deep Research modes (ChatGPT, Gemini, and to a lesser extent Claude's web-search/research mode) run many hidden tool calls (web searches, page fetches) before producing a final answer; only the final rendered text is visible to a content script. defaultMultiplier is applied to the visible response's effective output-token count before the normal cost/water/energy math runs, as a single rough proxy for that invisible work. Derived from a real published cost breakdown for Gemini Deep Research (see researchMode.sourceUrl): a standard task's total real cost (~$0.95 inference + ~$1.12-2.24 Search grounding, call it ~$2.5) divided by what our own calc() would compute from tokenizing just the visible ~60K-token final report at Gemini 3.1 Pro's normal output rate (~$0.72) gives ~3.5x; rounded to 4x. This is much lower than an earlier unverified 10-20x guess floated before this data was found — trust this number over that one. Applied identically across providers/sites for lack of anything more specific; OpenAI's Deep Research uses a different, cheaper search-tool cost structure so 4x may still be off in either direction for it.

claude-haiku-4-5.notes: No Anthropic-published or independently-measured water/energy figure exists for this model. Derived: public-estimate baseline (45 mL / 1000 output tokens, pre-2025 widely-cited figure, no vendor methodology) scaled down by this model's output price relative to claude-sonnet-5's ($5 vs $15/MTok = 0.33x) as a rough compute-intensity proxy, then water/energy cross-derived via Google's measured Wh:mL ratio. Confidence: low.
claude-haiku-4-5.verified: pricing confirmed via web search 2026-07-19 (unchanged from PRD); water/energy are derived estimates, not independently verified.

claude-sonnet-5.notes: No Anthropic-published or independently-measured water/energy figure exists for this model. Water uses the generic public-estimate baseline (45 mL / 1000 output tokens); energy cross-derived via Google's measured Wh:mL ratio. Used as the reference point for scaling claude-haiku-4-5 and claude-opus-4-8. Confidence: low. PRICING NOTE: $2.00/$10.00 is Anthropic's introductory rate, expires 2026-08-31; standard rate becomes $3.00/$15.00 after that date. This file's `lastVerified` predates the switch — revisit before/at Sept 1 2026.
claude-sonnet-5.verified: pricing confirmed via web search 2026-07-19 (unchanged from PRD, intro-rate window confirmed active); water/energy are derived estimates.

claude-opus-4-8.notes: No Anthropic-published or independently-measured water/energy figure exists for this model. Derived: public-estimate baseline scaled up by this model's output price relative to claude-sonnet-5's ($25 vs $15/MTok = 1.67x), then cross-derived via Google's Wh:mL ratio. Fast Mode pricing ($10/$50) not modeled separately. Confidence: low.
claude-opus-4-8.verified: pricing confirmed via web search 2026-07-19 (unchanged from PRD, Fast Mode $10/$50 also confirmed but not modeled here); water/energy are derived estimates.

gpt-5.notes: Energy is a real independently-measured figure: University of Rhode Island AI Lab metered GPU power directly for a medium-length ~1000-token response, average 18.35 Wh (range up to 40 Wh) — not OpenAI-disclosed, but not fabricated either, it's the strongest non-Gemini figure available. Water has no independent source; cross-derived from the measured energy via Google's Wh:mL ratio. Confidence: medium (energy), low (water).
gpt-5.verified: pricing confirmed via web search 2026-07-19 (unchanged from PRD's $0.625/$5.00 Azure-hosted rate; other hosts run up to $1.25 input); energy figure confirmed via web search 2026-07-19 (matches PRD's ~18Wh avg / 40Wh max).

gpt-5-4.notes: No independent water/energy study exists specifically for GPT-5.4 yet. Carried over GPT-5's measured energy/water figures as a placeholder assumption (same family, no evidence either direction) — replace as soon as a GPT-5.4-specific figure is published. Confidence: low.
gpt-5-4.verified: pricing confirmed via web search 2026-07-19 (unchanged from PRD's $2.50/$15.00); water/energy are carried-over placeholders, not GPT-5.4-specific.

gemini-3-flash.notes: Google's disclosed figure (0.24 Wh, 0.26 mL per ~600-token median prompt) is a blended median across the whole Gemini Apps fleet, not published per-model. Applied identically here and to gemini-3-1-pro pending a per-model breakdown from Google. This is nonetheless the single most rigorous, methodology-disclosed figure in this file. Confidence: medium (real disclosure, but not model-specific).
gemini-3-flash.verified: pricing confirmed via web search 2026-07-19 (unchanged from PRD's $0.50/$3.00); water/energy figure confirmed via web search 2026-07-19 against Google's Aug 2025 paper (unchanged).

gemini-3-1-pro.notes: Same blended fleet-median figure as gemini-3-flash — see that entry's note. Pricing rises to $4.00/$18.00 above 200K context tokens, not modeled here (base-tier rate used). Confidence: medium (real disclosure, but not model-specific).
gemini-3-1-pro.verified: pricing confirmed via web search 2026-07-19 (base tier unchanged from PRD's $2.00/$12.00; >200K-context step-up to $4/$18 newly confirmed, not previously in PRD); water/energy figure confirmed via web search 2026-07-19 (unchanged).

deepseek-v3.notes: No DeepSeek-V3-specific water/energy study found. Energy borrowed from the same URI Lab study's measurement of DeepSeek R1 (20.90 Wh avg, ~1000-token response, same provider/lineage though a different model) as the closest available real figure; water cross-derived via Google's Wh:mL ratio. IMPORTANT: DeepSeek has scheduled deepseek-chat/deepseek-reasoner (the V3-era API models) for deprecation on 2026-07-24 — this entry and deepseek.js's fallback default will need updating shortly after this file's lastVerified date. Confidence: low.
deepseek-v3.verified: pricing confirmed via web search 2026-07-19 (unchanged from PRD's $0.27/$1.10); deprecation date is new information not in the PRD, flagged above. Water/energy are derived, not DeepSeek-V3-specific.

deepseek-v4-flash.notes: No DeepSeek-V4-Flash-specific water/energy study found. Derived from deepseek-v3's borrowed R1 energy figure, scaled down by this model's output price relative to deepseek-v3's ($0.28 vs $1.10/MTok = 0.2545x) as a compute-intensity proxy. Cached-input rate ($0.0028/MTok) not modeled — cache hits will read as more expensive than they really are. Confidence: low.
deepseek-v4-flash.verified: pricing confirmed via web search 2026-07-19 (unchanged from PRD's $0.14/$0.28 cache-miss rate, cached-input rate $0.0028 also confirmed but not modeled); water/energy are derived, not DeepSeek-V4-specific.

gpt-image-1-5.notes: OpenAI genuinely tokenizes generated images — 272/1056/4160 output tokens for low/medium/high quality at 1024x1024 on gpt-image-1.5 ($32/1M output tokens); this entry uses the medium-quality figure (1056 tok = $0.0338/image). inputPricePerMTok ($5.00/1M text input tokens) is OpenAI's own published rate for this model, not borrowed from an unrelated text model as v3 did. energyWhPerUnit/waterMlPerUnit use Bertazzini et al. 2025/2026 (arXiv:2506.17016, 'The Hidden Cost of an Image'), a real GPU-metered study of 17 open text-to-image models: their 'standard quality' tier (~3 Wh/image, comparable modern diffusion/transformer models) is the closest available real analog — no OpenAI-specific figure is published. Water cross-derived from that Wh figure via Google's measured Wh:mL ratio (0.24 Wh : 0.26 mL). gpt-image-1 (the model originally scoped) was retired 2026-10-23, so this uses its successor instead. Confidence: medium (real, verified cost inputs), medium-low (energy/water — real measured study, but not this exact model).
gpt-image-1-5.verified: pricing confirmed via web search 2026-08-30 ($0.0338/image output + $5.00/1M text input, both OpenAI's own published rates); energy/water switched from a borrowed-text-model derivation to Bertazzini et al.'s directly-measured image-generation study, confirmed via web search 2026-08-30.

imagen-4-standard.notes: Google bills Imagen as a flat per-image price ($0.02/0.04/0.06 for Fast/Standard/Ultra), not tokenized and with no separate input-token charge — inputPricePerMTok is intentionally omitted (defaults to 0) rather than fabricating a cost Google doesn't bill. tokenEquivalentPerUnit is display-only now: $0.04 / gemini-3-1-pro's $12/MTok output rate = 3333, shown in the card's token-equivalent chip but no longer used for water/energy math. energyWhPerUnit/waterMlPerUnit use the same Bertazzini et al. real-measured-image-generation basis as gpt-image-1-5 (see that entry's notes) — no Imagen-specific figure is published by Google, so this is the best available real analog rather than an unrelated text model's rate. Confidence: low-medium.
imagen-4-standard.verified: pricing confirmed via web search 2026-08-30 (unchanged, $0.04/image standard tier); energy/water switched from borrowed gemini-3-1-pro text rate to Bertazzini et al.'s directly-measured image-generation study, confirmed via web search 2026-08-30.

veo-3-1-fast.notes: Google bills Veo per second, flat, no separate input-token charge (inputPricePerMTok omitted, same reasoning as imagen-4-standard). pricePerUnit corrected to $0.15/sec (Google's own current Gemini API rate for Veo 3.1 Fast at 720p/1080p — v3's $0.12 was a stale blog estimate); tokenEquivalentPerUnit is display-only, recomputed to match ($0.15 / gemini-3-1-pro's $12/MTok = 12500). energyWhPerUnit/waterMlPerUnit use 'Lights, Camera, Carbon: Architectural Scaling Laws for Video Generation Energy Consumption' (arXiv:2607.04553), which estimates Veo 3 (not 3.1, but same family — closest available) at 19.8-43.4 Wh (mean 30.8 Wh) per 8-second 720p clip via an architectural scaling-law fit to real API latency, not direct GPU metering. 30.8 Wh / 8s = 3.85 Wh/sec; water cross-derived via Google's measured Wh:mL ratio. This replaces v3's coincidentally-similar but methodologically-unfounded borrowed-text-model number with a real, Veo-targeted academic estimate. Each Veo generation caps at 8 seconds — a 9s+ video needs multiple generations; this per-second rate still applies linearly, matching Google's own per-second billing. Confidence: medium (real, model-targeted estimate; API-latency-based, not direct measurement, and Veo 3 not 3.1 specifically).
veo-3-1-fast.verified: pricing corrected via web search 2026-08-30 (Google's Gemini API pricing page: $0.15/sec, not v3's $0.12 estimate); energy/water switched from borrowed gemini-3-1-pro text rate to a Veo-3-targeted academic estimate, confirmed via web search 2026-08-30.

researchMode.notes: See _meta.waterEnergyMethodology.researchMode for the full derivation. Applied to effective output tokens (cost + water + energy alike) for any response detected as a Deep-Research-style multi-step answer, uniformly across sites for lack of per-provider data. Confidence: low-medium (grounded in one real cost breakdown for one provider, extrapolated to all).

carbonIntensity.notes: Global average CO2 intensity of electricity generation: 445 g CO2/kWh, the latest full-year actual per IEA's Electricity 2025 report (IEA forecasts this declining toward ~400 g by 2027 as clean generation grows worldwide, but that's a moving global blended average, not something this file re-derives per release). No AI provider discloses which grid(s), datacenter(s), or PUE actually powered a given inference request, so — same treatment as researchMode's multiplier — one global constant is applied uniformly to every model's/mediaModel's already-estimated energyWh rather than a provider- or region-specific factor, which isn't public. Carbon is therefore always a straight derivation of a response's energy estimate, never an independently sourced figure of its own; its confidence can never exceed the energy figure it's derived from. Confidence: low (uniform global proxy, not model- or datacenter-specific).
carbonIntensity.verified: figure confirmed via web search 2026-08-30 against IEA's Electricity 2025 report (445 g CO2/kWh for 2024, the latest actual).
